description: The plot illustrates how accuracy varies with initial confidence and includes three series with error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.81 to 0.99 with tick labels shown at irregular intervals (including 0.81, 0.82, 0.84–0.89, 0.90–0.97, 0.98, 0.99). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0, and shows regularly spaced tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The blue series (solid line with circular markers) starts near 1.00 at 0.81, stays in the high range around ~0.88–0.97 across the x-axis, dips to about 0.86 around 0.95, and ends near 0.98 at 0.99. The orange series labeled “Δ Accuracy” (dashed line with diamond markers) begins around 0.46 at 0.81, generally declines with fluctuations (e.g., around 0.14 at 0.86, about 0.37 at 0.88, about 0.30 at 0.93), and finishes near 0.04 at 0.99. The green series labeled “Initial Accuracy” (dash-dot line with square markers) starts around 0.54 at 0.81, varies between roughly ~0.52 and ~0.76 through most mid-range confidences (e.g., about 0.75 at 0.86 and about 0.65 at 0.91), then rises toward the right side to about 0.82 at 0.98 and about 0.94 at 0.99; all three series include vertical error bars at each x-position.
